title: Brick Schema
description: Uniform metadata schema for buildings: a vocabulary for describing the points (sensors, setpoints, commands, statuses, alarms), equipment (AHUs, chillers, pumps, VAVs, network devices, etc.), and their relationships (hasPoint/isPointOf, hasPart/isPartOf, feeds/isFedBy, hasUnit via QUDT) in building automation and IoT deployments. Widely used in the building controls / smart buildings community.
publisher: Brick Consortium (UC Berkeley, with industry and academic contributors); ontology hosted at ontology.brickschema.org

models.name: CO2_Level_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - CO2_Level_Sensor
models.description: Measures the concentration of CO2 in air (brick:CO2_Level_Sensor's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology). A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:CO2_Level_Sensor, hierarchy: CO2_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: Collection
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Collection
models.description: A logical grouping of points, equipment or other entities that doesn't correspond to a physical or system relationship (brick:Collection and its subclasses, e.g. Automation_Collection). INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN: Collection has no Brick-native membership property in any real Brick example checked (examples/collection/collection.ttl, examples/chiller-system/chiller-plant.ttl, examples/iaq_sensor_deployment) -- every real Collection instance found expresses its membership via RealEstateCore's rec:includes / rec:hasMember, not a Brick property. One of Brick's own example files even comments on this directly. This schema is therefore published as a placeholder (identity + brickClass only, no members) rather than either inventing a non-Brick property or silently omitting Collection altogether. A membership Relationship should be added once the planned RealEstateCore candidate exists for it to point to.

models.name: Equipment
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Equipment
models.description: A physical piece of equipment in a building's mechanical, electrical or IT systems: an air handling unit, chiller, pump, VAV box, thermostat, network device, etc. (brick:Equipment and its subclasses, Brick Schema). Modeled generically -- see the brickClass property -- rather than as hundreds of separate entity types.

models.name: Occupancy_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Occupancy_Sensor
models.description: Detects the presence or count of occupants. Unlike the other five classes in this batch, Occupancy_Sensor has no brick:hasSubstance in the source ontology (occupancy isn't a property of a substance/medium the way temperature or a gas concentration is) -- this schema therefore has no hasSubstance property at all, rather than an empty or null one. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Occupancy_Sensor, hierarchy: Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: PM10_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - PM10_Sensor
models.description: Measures the concentration of PM10 (particulate matter, <=10 micrometers) in air. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:PM10_Sensor, hierarchy: Particulate_Matter_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: PM2.5_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - PM2.5_Sensor
models.description: Measures the concentration of PM2.5 (fine particulate matter, <=2.5 micrometers) in air. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:PM2.5_Sensor, hierarchy: Particulate_Matter_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: Point
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Point
models.description: A telemetry point exposed by a piece of building Equipment or associated with a Location: a sensor, setpoint, command, status, alarm or parameter (brick:Point and its subclasses, Brick Schema). This candidate models Point generically -- see the brickClass property -- rather than as hundreds of separate entity types.

models.name: Relative_Humidity_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Relative_Humidity_Sensor
models.description: Measures the relative humidity of air. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Relative_Humidity_Sensor, hierarchy: Humidity_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: System
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - System
models.description: A functional grouping of equipment that together provide a building service, e.g. an HVAC system or a chilled water system (brick:System and its subclasses). INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN: System has no Brick-native membership property in any real Brick example checked (examples/collection/collection.ttl, examples/chiller-system/chiller-plant.ttl, examples/iaq_sensor_deployment) -- every real System instance found expresses its membership via RealEstateCore's rec:includes / rec:hasMember, not a Brick property. One of Brick's own example files even comments on this directly. This schema is therefore published as a placeholder (identity + brickClass only, no members) rather than either inventing a non-Brick property or silently omitting System altogether. A membership Relationship should be added once the planned RealEstateCore candidate exists for it to point to.

models.name: Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor
models.description: A temperature sensor for the air within an HVAC zone -- one specific member of Brick's broader Temperature_Sensor family (which also includes e.g. Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor, Discharge_Air_Temperature_Sensor). Modeled as its own class here because this is the exact leaf class in the real example data (a thermostat's zone sensor); the other family members share the same property shape and could be added the same way. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor, hierarchy: Air_Temperature_Sensor -> Temperature_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

title: EDINT Infrastructure Ontology (Ontología de Infraestructura)
description: Vocabulary for representing a municipality's public and private infrastructure facilities (educational, cultural, social, sports and health centers, on-street and off-street parking, shared-bicycle stations) together with the sensors, observations, violations, management roles and organizations involved in operating and monitoring them. Reuses SOSA/SSN (sensors and observations), GeoSPARQL (geometry), schema.org and Dublin Core.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) as technical developer

models.name: AccessObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - AccessObservation
models.description: Observation carried out at any entrance to a municipal facility. This includes pedestrian or vehicle access (edintinf:AccessObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: AccessSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - AccessSensor
models.description: A device that records the access of people or vehicles. This could be an LPR (license plate recognition) camera, a building entrance door sensor, or other similar devices (edintinf:AccessSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor).

models.name: BikeSharingStation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - BikeSharingStation
models.description: A Facility specialization for shared-bicycle stations (edintinf:EstacionBicicleta). Like Parking, the source ontology defines no attributes of its own beyond those inherited from Facility. Check for overlap with any existing bike-sharing SDM model before promoting this candidate.

models.name: CountingObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - CountingObservation
models.description: Observation on the number of people or vehicles that a sensor counts (edintinf:CountingObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: CountingSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - CountingSensor
models.description: A device that records the number of people or vehicles that it observes (edintinf:CountingSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor).

models.name: Facility
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Facility
models.description: It refers to service buildings (public or private), leisure areas, commercial areas or any other element that directly affects mobility, acting as a focus of attraction for persons or vehicles. Source: EDINT Infrastructure Ontology (edintinf:Facility).

models.name: ManagementRole
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - ManagementRole
models.description: The role that the municipal administration or one of its departments plays in the management of a municipal facility. This may include ownership, maintenance, security, among others (edintinf:ManagementRole).

models.name: ObservationPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - ObservationPoint
models.description: Points where access or counting observations can be made using sensors (edintinf:ObservationPoint). The source ontology defines no attributes of its own beyond location; it is the target of the Facility.hasObservationPoint relationship.

models.name: Organization
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Organization
models.description: Any public or private organization that owns or manages an element of the infrastructure (edintinf:Organization). NOTE: check for overlap with the existing official Smart Data Models 'dataModel.Organization' subject before promoting this candidate.

models.name: Parking
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Parking
models.description: A Facility specialization for on-street and off-street parking areas. The source ontology (edintinf:Parking) defines no attributes beyond those inherited from Facility; it is distinguished only by its NGSI-LD type and, typically, its infrastructureType value. NOTE: this concept is likely to overlap with the already-existing official Smart Data Models 'dataModel.Parking' subject (e.g. OffStreetParking/OnStreetParking) — check for duplication before promoting this candidate.

models.name: Violation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Violation
models.description: Non-compliance or violation of traffic or access rules, road laws or local ordinances by a person or a driver or owner of a vehicle (edintinf:Violation).

title: SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology, as demonstrated by the EDINT Tourism repository
description: Vocabulary for representing tourism accommodation establishments (hotels, guest houses, aparthotels) and historical/cultural resources (fortified palaces, amphitheatres, aqueducts, and 40+ related types), together with their location, contact points, booking channels, ratings and descriptions. Drawn from SEGITTUR's Core Tourism Ontology (estur:), a large (388-class) reference model for a Network of Tourism Sector Ontologies serving Spain's future Intelligent Destination Platform (PID).
publisher: SEGITTUR (Sociedad Estatal para la Gestión de la Innovación y las Tecnologías Turísticas), with the Ontology Engineering Group (Universidad Politécnica de Madrid), Globaldit and Gnoss as technical developers

models.name: Alcazar
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Alcazar
models.description: Alcazar (fortified palace), a specialization of HistoricalOrCulturalResource (estur:HistoricalOrCulturalResource, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology) — one of 43 such subclasses in the full ontology (others include Museum, Castle, Cathedral, Monastery, etc.), of which this candidate only covers the three demonstrated with real example data. NOTE: the source repository's example data uses the misspellings 'Amphiteatre' and 'Acueduct'; the authoritative ontology spells these 'Amphitheatre' and 'Aqueduct', which are used here.

models.name: Amphitheatre
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Amphitheatre
models.description: Amphitheatre, a specialization of HistoricalOrCulturalResource (estur:HistoricalOrCulturalResource, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology) — one of 43 such subclasses in the full ontology (others include Museum, Castle, Cathedral, Monastery, etc.), of which this candidate only covers the three demonstrated with real example data. NOTE: the source repository's example data uses the misspellings 'Amphiteatre' and 'Acueduct'; the authoritative ontology spells these 'Amphitheatre' and 'Aqueduct', which are used here.

models.name: Aparthotel
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Aparthotel
models.description: Aparthotel, a specialization of AccommodationEstablishment (estur:AccommodationEstablishment via TourismOrRelatedFacility, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source repository's README uses the misspelling 'AccomodationEstablishment' (single 'm'); the authoritative ontology spells it 'AccommodationEstablishment' (double 'm'), which is used throughout this candidate.

models.name: Aqueduct
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Aqueduct
models.description: Aqueduct, a specialization of HistoricalOrCulturalResource (estur:HistoricalOrCulturalResource, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology) — one of 43 such subclasses in the full ontology (others include Museum, Castle, Cathedral, Monastery, etc.), of which this candidate only covers the three demonstrated with real example data. NOTE: the source repository's example data uses the misspellings 'Amphiteatre' and 'Acueduct'; the authoritative ontology spells these 'Amphitheatre' and 'Aqueduct', which are used here.

models.name: BookingChannel
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - BookingChannel
models.description: A channel through which a tourism resource, service or organisation can be booked (estur:BookingChannel, a ContactPoint subclass, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: ContactPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - ContactPoint
models.description: A means of contacting a tourism entity or organisation (estur:ContactPoint, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: Description
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Description
models.description: A textual description of a tourism entity (estur:Description, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: Hostal
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Hostal
models.description: Hostal (Spanish guest house), a specialization of AccommodationEstablishment (estur:AccommodationEstablishment via TourismOrRelatedFacility, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source repository's README uses the misspelling 'AccomodationEstablishment' (single 'm'); the authoritative ontology spells it 'AccommodationEstablishment' (double 'm'), which is used throughout this candidate.

models.name: Hotel
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Hotel
models.description: Hotel, a specialization of AccommodationEstablishment (estur:AccommodationEstablishment via TourismOrRelatedFacility, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source repository's README uses the misspelling 'AccomodationEstablishment' (single 'm'); the authoritative ontology spells it 'AccommodationEstablishment' (double 'm'), which is used throughout this candidate.

models.name: Location
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Location
models.description: The location of a tourism entity (accommodation, historical/cultural resource, etc.), modeled as a standalone, referenceable resource, matching the source ontology's own design (estur:Location, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: Rating
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Rating
models.description: A rating of a tourism resource, service or organisation (estur:Rating, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source ontology's own SHACL shapes define a different, incompatible field set for Rating (bookingValue/googleReviewValue/tripAdvisorValue as floats, plus a flat 'stars' integer directly on Hotel) that does not match either the OWL property definitions or any real example data found. This candidate follows ratingUnit/ratingValue because that is what the real, published open-data examples (and the OWL definitions) actually use — check with SEGITTUR before assuming either naming scheme is final.

title: ERA ERADIS (documents/certification register)
description: ERADIS is one of four registers (alongside RINF, ERATV, EVR) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3 -- see era-rinf's standard-metadata.yaml for the shared ontology-wide context. ERADIS covers the certification and compliance-documentation side of the railway authorisation processes: Certificates (safety certificates for railway undertakings), Conformity Assessment Body (CAB) evidence, assessment/audit checks and restrictions, Certification Level Documents, EC Declarations of Verification/Conformity, document sets, validity constraints on certificates/decisions, and references to the Technical Specifications for Interoperability (TSIs) those checks are performed against.

models.name: CABAddition
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CABAddition
models.description: CAB assessed addition (era:CABAddition's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): An additionally allowed Option, Added Function which was confirmed by a CAB Inherits attributes from era:Restriction (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABAssessmentCheck
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CABAssessmentCheck
models.description: CAB Assessment Check (era:CABAssessmentCheck's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A compliance check as executed by a Conformity Assessment Body. The class can be used NoBo, DeBo and/or AsBo checks. Inherits attributes from era:Compliance (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABAuditCheck
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CABAuditCheck
models.description: CAB Audit Check (era:CABAuditCheck's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A compliance observation as executed by a Conformity Assessment Body in an audit. The class can be used NoBo, DeBo and/or AsBo checks. Inherits attributes from era:Compliance (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABCertificate
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CABCertificate
models.description: Certificate from a CAB (era:CABCertificate's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A `vpa:EvidenceDocument` from a Conformity Assessment Body examining any other reference than a TSI or its annexes. Inherits attributes from era:EvidenceDocument (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABEvidence
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CABEvidence
models.description: Evidence from a CAB (era:CABEvidence's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A `era:DocumentSet` which mainly contains Certification Level Documents or Certificates of Conformity from a Conformity Assessment Body. Inherits attributes from era:DocumentSet/era:Evidence (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABRestriction
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CABRestriction
models.description: CAB restriction (era:CABRestriction's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A Restriction which was issued by a CAB Inherits attributes from era:Restriction (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: Certificate
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - Certificate
models.description: Certificate (era:Certificate's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Base class for those Certificates in the ERADIS register, which allow a IOD/SD described process. Inherits attributes from era:Permission (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CertificationLevelDocument
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CertificationLevelDocument
models.description: Certification Level Document (era:CertificationLevelDocument's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Certification Level Document, as issued by a NoBo in the process of its certification/verification activities [RFU-STR-001]. The class can be reused as well for DeBo and AsBo certificates. Inherits attributes from era:EvidenceDocument (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: DocumentSet
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - DocumentSet
models.description: Application Document Set (era:DocumentSet's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A collection of documents belonging together, as they contain - as a set - evidence in an ERA process like registration or authorisation. Inherits attributes from era:Evidence (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: ECDeclaration
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - ECDeclaration
models.description: EC Declaration of Verification/Conformity (era:ECDeclaration's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): EC Declaration of Verification/Conformity/Suitability for Use, as issued by an Applicant in the process of certification/verification activities for IC's or subsystems. Inherits attributes from era:EvidenceDocument (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: ForbiddenAssessmentConstraint
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - ForbiddenAssessmentConstraint
models.description: Forbidden assessment constraint (era:ForbiddenAssessmentConstraint's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A validity constraint signalling that the combination of CLD type and assessment module is structurally not permitted under this TSI.

models.name: MaxDurationConstraint
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - MaxDurationConstraint
models.description: Maximum duration constraint (era:MaxDurationConstraint's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A validity constraint that imposes an upper bound on the CLD validity period. Being a subclass of time:DurationDescription, it uses time:years (and potentially time:months, time:days) to express the maximum allowed duration.

models.name: TechnicalSpecForInteroperability
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - TechnicalSpecForInteroperability
models.description: Technical Specification for Interoperability (era:TechnicalSpecForInteroperability's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Technical Specification for Interoperability Inherits attributes from era:Requirement (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: UnlimitedValidityConstraint
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - UnlimitedValidityConstraint
models.description: Unlimited validity constraint (era:UnlimitedValidityConstraint's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A validity constraint signalling that the CLD has no expiry — no end date or duration should be specified.

title: ERA ERATV (European Register of Authorised Vehicle Types)
description: ERATV is one of four registers (alongside RINF, ERADIS, EVR) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3 -- see the era-rinf candidate's standard-metadata.yaml for the shared ontology-wide context. ERATV itself covers authorised railway VEHICLE TYPES (as opposed to EVR, which registers individual vehicles): the vehicle type's technical characteristics (dimensions, mass, braking performance, gauging, ETCS/GSM-R/ATO on-board equipment, noise, energy supply compatibility, ...), its per-configuration variants (VehicleTypeConfiguration / VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet, since a single type can be authorised in several technical configurations, e.g. different energy supply systems or ETCS on-board versions), and the type-authorisation process itself (VehicleTypeAuthorisation, its Application, Case, compliance Check, and Restriction).

models.name: VehicleType
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleType
models.description:
Vehicle Type (era:VehicleType's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A vehicle type that has been authorized to operate on the EU railway infrastructure. Type means a vehicle type defining the basic design characteristics of the vehicle as covered by a type or design examination certificate described in the relevant verification module.

Basic design characteristics means the parameters that are used to identify the vehicle type as specified in the issued vehicle type authorisation and recorded in the European Register of Authorised Vehicle Types ('ERATV').

The above mentioned certificate should be documented using era:certificate.

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisation
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisation
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisation's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): (16) the decision issued by the authorising entity based on reasonable assurance that the applicant and the entities involved in the design,
manufacture, verification and validation of the vehicle type have fulfilled their obligations and responsibilities in order to ensure conformity with the essential
requirements of the applicable legislation enabling that a vehicle manufactured according to this design may be placed on the market and may be used safely in the
area of use of the vehicle type according to the conditions for use of the vehicle and other restrictions, when applicable, specified in the vehicle type authorisation
and to be applied to all vehicle authorised in conformity to this type; Inherits attributes from era:Permission (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Case (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The request, as submitted by the Applicant in line with (EU)2018/545, to allow the vehicle type authorisation and/or the vehicle authorisation for placing on the market.
The application consists of one or more authorisation cases as described in Art. 14 of (EU)2018/545, and for authorisations before the Fourth Railway Package, a HistoricalAuthorisationCase must be used.

The outcome of the application process is a `era:VehicleAuthorisation` or `era:VehicleTypeAuthorisation`. Inherits attributes from era:Request (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationCase
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationCase
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Case (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationCase's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The process, as selected by the Applicant in line with (EU)2018/545, allowing the vehicle type authorisation and/or the vehicle authorisation for placing on the market.
The type of authorisation cases are described in Art. 14 of (EU)2018/545, and for authorisations before the Fourth Railway Package, a HistoricalAuthorisationCase must be used.

Each authorisation case supports a VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication and is determined by exactly one VehicleType, and a set of Vehicles, which can be empty in some cases.

For authorisations before the (EU)2018/545 legislation, use `era:VehicleAuthorisationCase. Inherits attributes from era:Case (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationCheck
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationCheck
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Compliance Check (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationCheck's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A verification result as executed by a competent body on a section of a legal reference. The check can be positive or negative, and in the latter case, a restriction is expected.

This Class is used to improve the link between verification outcomes and the verified scope of that process, and support its structured documentation. Inherits attributes from era:Compliance (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationRestriction
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationRestriction
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Restriction (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationRestriction's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Restrictions, like coded and non-coded conditions for use, to be taken into account in the context of a Vehicle (Type) Authorisation.

The restrictions are recorded by the Authorising Entities, possibly deduced during underlying verification and certification processes by competent bodies, and if possible are documented with a link
to the legal reference and sections therein.

In most cases, the Restriction will be dependent of a VehicleTypeConfiguration. Inherits attributes from era:Restriction (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet
models.description: Vehicle type configuration parameter set (era:VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Stub class linking a VehicleTypeConfiguration (`era:forConfiguration`) with parameters of the VehicleType that depend on that configuration.

models.name: VehicleTypeConfiguration
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeConfiguration
models.description: Vehicle type configuration (era:VehicleTypeConfiguration's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The combination of supported Gauge, Energy Systems and/or CCO Systems for a vehicle type

title: ERA EVR (European Vehicle Register)
description: EVR is the last of the four registers (alongside RINF, ERATV, ERADIS) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3 -- see era-rinf's standard-metadata.yaml for the shared ontology-wide context. EVR registers individual VEHICLES (as opposed to ERATV, which authorises vehicle TYPES): each vehicle's identity and technical data as manufactured (European Vehicle Number, keeper, owner, ECM, manufacturing details), its Vehicle Keeper Marking (VKM), national-level registration properties defined by individual member states, and the registration process itself (VehicleRegistration, its Application, Case, compliance Check, and Restriction) plus the closely related vehicle (not vehicle-type) authorisation-for-placing-in-service process (VehicleAuthorisation, Case, Notification).

models.name: ERTMSErrorChangeRequest
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - ERTMSErrorChangeRequest
models.description: ERTMS error change request (era:ERTMSErrorChangeRequest's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): SKOS concept representing a change request (CR) classified as an error in the ERTMS specifications and analysed by the Agency to identify whether it may prevent the system from providing normal service under Article 10 of the CCS TSI.

models.name: NationalRegistrationProperty
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - NationalRegistrationProperty
models.description: National Registration Property (era:NationalRegistrationProperty's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A property defined at national level by a member state for vehicle registration purposes. Each member state may define its own set of such properties, identified by a national property identifier string. This class avoids creating individual era: predicates for each member-state-specific registration field. The member state is determined by the registeringMemberState of the parent VehicleRegistrationCase.

models.name: Vehicle
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - Vehicle
models.description: Vehicle (era:Vehicle's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A specific vehicle or wagon able and allowed to operate over railway infrastructure.

models.name: VehicleAuthorisation
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleAuthorisation
models.description:
Vehicle Authorisation for Placing on the Market (era:VehicleAuthorisation's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): (15) the decision issued by the authorising entity based on a reasonable assurance that the applicant and the entities involved in the design,
manufacture, verification and validation of the vehicle have fulfilled their respective obligations and responsibilities in order to ensure conformity with essential
requirements of the applicable legislation or to ensure conformity with the authorised type enabling that the vehicle may be placed on the market and may be used safely in the
area of use according to the conditions for use and other restrictions, when applicable, specified in the vehicle authorisation and in the vehicle type authorisation; Inherits attributes from era:Permission (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleAuthorisationCase
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleAuthorisationCase
models.description:
Vehicle APIS Case (era:VehicleAuthorisationCase's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The process allowing the vehicle authorisation for placing in service (APIS).

This authorisation case supported a Vehicle Application for APIS and was determined by exactly one set of Vehicles and if available a VehicleType.

For the Authorisation as per EU 2018/545, use era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationCase, which covers all authorisations types under that legislation. Inherits attributes from era:Case (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleAuthorisationNotification
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleAuthorisationNotification
models.description:
Vehicle Authorisation Notification (era:VehicleAuthorisationNotification's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The notification, as submitted by the Applicant in line with (EU)2018/545, informs the authorising entity of the vehicle(s set) to be updated according to Article 16.
The notification consists of one case as described in Art. 16 of (EU)2018/545, containing the vehicle type and EVNs, and linking to the required Evidence.

The outcome of the notification process is an added comment in the  `era:VehicleAuthorisation`, if accepted by the Authorising Entity. Inherits attributes from era:Request (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleKeeperMarking
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleKeeperMarking
models.description: Vehicle Keeper Marking (era:VehicleKeeperMarking's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The class used to relate a Vehicle Keeper Marking (VKM) properties for the purpose of the VKM register. Inherits attributes from era:OrganisationRole (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleRegistration
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleRegistration
models.description:
Vehicle Registration (era:VehicleRegistration's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Vehicle Registration serves to ensure traceability of vehicles and their history: vehicles should be registered under a European vehicle number in a vehicle register. Each
member state designated a registration entity responsible for the registering of vehicles and the processing and update of information in relation to vehicles that entity has registered in the European Vehicle Register.

A vehicle registration groups the information for a (set of) vehicle(s) as in Appendix 4 of Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1614 of 25 October 2018. Inherits attributes from era:Permission (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleRegistrationApplication
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleRegistrationApplication
models.description:
Application for Vehicle Registration (era:VehicleRegistrationApplication's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Keepers should fill in an application for registration with the required information (Appendix 4 of EVR Decision).  A keeper shall submit an application for registration through
the European Vehicle Register to a Member State of its choice within the area of use of the vehicle.

A VehicleRegistrationApplication traces the state of this process, links to the RegistrationCase(s), and a registration entity independent of any railway undertaking which
will be responsible for the processing of the applications and updating of data in the European Vehicle Register. Inherits attributes from era:Request (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleRegistrationCase
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleRegistrationCase
models.description:
Vehicle Registration Case (era:VehicleRegistrationCase's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Vehicle Registrations can be created and modified using a specific Registration Case as listed in `3.2.2.   Registration cases` of the EVR Decision.

Each registration case will have as its scope:
- a set of vehicles of which the registration needs creating/updating.
- if present, the authorisation delivered for these vehicles and/or vehicle type to which they belong. Inherits attributes from era:Case (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleRegistrationCheck
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleRegistrationCheck
models.description:
Vehicle Registration Compliance Check (era:VehicleRegistrationCheck's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A verification result as executed by a competent body on a section of a legal reference. The check can be optional, positive or negative, and in the latter case, a restriction is expected.

This Class is used to improve the link between verification outcomes and the verified scope of that process, and support its structured documentation.

It must be used in the context of the Vehicle Registration process. Inherits attributes from era:Compliance (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleRegistrationRestriction
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleRegistrationRestriction
models.description: Vehicle Registration Restriction (era:VehicleRegistrationRestriction's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): An `era:Restriction` which originates from a compliance check during the Vehicle's Registration. Inherits attributes from era:Restriction (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleSeries
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleSeries
models.description: Series of Vehicles (era:VehicleSeries's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Collection of Vehicles belonging together, for instance in the scope of an Authorisation or Registration Case.

models.name: VehicleSet
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleSet
models.description: Vehicle Set (era:VehicleSet's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A set of vehicles together forming the Scope of a registration/authorisation case or involved as on whole in another process.

title: ERA RINF (Register of Infrastructure)
description: RINF is one of four registers (alongside ERATV, ERADIS, EVR) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3. RINF itself covers the physical and topological railway infrastructure of the EU network: operational points, tracks (running tracks and sidings), sections of line, tunnels, bridges, platforms, level crossings, switches, signals, electrification (contact line systems, pantograph/phase-separation parameters), control-command and signalling (ETCS, Radio Block Centres, train detection systems, GSM-R), and the abstract network/topology graph model (NetElement, LinearElement, NetRelation, linear positioning systems) that ties physical assets to a navigable network representation. This candidate is the RINF sub-standard only; ERATV (authorised vehicle types), ERADIS (authorisation/certification documents), and EVR (vehicle register) are separate sub-standards of the same ontology, planned as later candidates under their own standards/ folders (era-eratv, era-eradis, era-evr) since they are distinct subject areas with their own entity graphs, sharing only a handful of admin classes (era:Body, era:OrganisationRole) with RINF.

models.name: Body

models.description: Body (era:Body's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Is an organisation or a physical person

models.name: Bridge
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - Bridge
models.description: Bridge (era:Bridge's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): It is a structure constructed for the exclusive purpose of carrying railroad traffic across an obstruction. It can be used for defining non-stopping areas, big metal mass, resistance to traffic load etc. Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: ContactLineSystem
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - ContactLineSystem
models.description: Contact Line System (era:ContactLineSystem's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): System that is used to transmit electrical energy to road or rail vehicles.

models.name: Document

models.name: ETCS

models.description: ETCS (era:ETCS's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): TSI compliant train protection system ERTMS / ETCS application level and baseline related to the track side equipment.

models.name: HABD

Hot Axle Box Detector (era:HABD's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A trackside Hot Axle Box Detector (HABD), necessary for the route compatibility check.
Specific for the French, Italian and Swedish networks Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: KilometricPost

Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: LevelCrossing
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - LevelCrossing
models.description: Level crossing (era:LevelCrossing's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A level crossing is an intersection where a railway line crosses a road or a path at the same level. It can be used for the implementation of the ETCS trackside or to identify potential collision scenarios Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: LinearElement
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - LinearElement
models.description: Linear Element (era:LinearElement's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Pieces of tracks composing the topology Inherits attributes from era:NetElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: LinearElementSection
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - LinearElementSection
models.description: Linear Element Section (era:LinearElementSection's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Represents a section of a linear element. Inherits attributes from era:LinearElement/era:NetElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: LinearPositioningSystem
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - LinearPositioningSystem
models.description:
Linear Positioning System (era:LinearPositioningSystem's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Represents a linear positioning system used for referencing positions on the network.
It can also represent a sequence of one or more sections of line, used for regular railway operations.

models.name: LinearPositioningSystemCoordinate
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - LinearPositioningSystemCoordinate
models.description: Linear Positioning System Coordinate (era:LinearPositioningSystemCoordinate's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Represents coordinates in a linear positioning system.

models.name: LinesideDistanceIndication
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - LinesideDistanceIndication
models.description:
Lineside indications of distance (era:LinesideDistanceIndication's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Frequency, appearance and positioning of a sign indicating distance as reference post. Two types of signs are normally available: kilometre post and hectometre post.
- A kilometre post is a lineside sign indicating the distance from a specific point, usually being the starting point of the railway line.
- A hectometre post is a lineside sign indicating a relative distance.

models.name: NetAreaReference
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - NetAreaReference

models.name: NetPointReference

models.description: Net Point Reference (era:NetPointReference's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Represents a point reference in the network. Inherits attributes from era:NetBasicReference/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: NonLinearElement

models.name: OperationalPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - OperationalPoint
models.description: Operational Point (era:OperationalPoint's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): An operational point (OP) means any location for train service operations, where train services may begin and end or change route, and where passenger or freight services may be provided; operational point also means any location at boundaries between Member States or infrastructure managers. Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: OrganisationRole

models.name: Orientation
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - Orientation
models.description: Orientation (era:Orientation's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Represents the orientation of a railway object in relation to a carrier linear element. It can be described by direction, orientation and side.

models.name: PlatformEdge
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - PlatformEdge
models.description: Platform edge (era:PlatformEdge's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Platform for the purpose of RINF is understood as a platform edge. A platform concerns only the part of the structure neighbouring to the track (interfaced with trains). Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: PrimaryLocation
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - PrimaryLocation
models.description:
Primary Location (era:PrimaryLocation's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Primary Location is a place used by IM to define a path for a train in TAF/TAP TSI framework/messages. This location is a rail point inside the rail network where train starts, ends, stops, or runs through or change line. This location must be managed by an Infrastructure Manager (IM) identified by company code.

Primary locations are identified by single and unique Primary Location codes. Primary location code is allocated based on processes defined by national entity. Primary location codes are used in any kind of TAF/TAP communication. Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: RadioBlockCenter
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - RadioBlockCenter
models.description:
Radio Block Center (era:RadioBlockCenter's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): ETCS trackside centralised unit controlling ETCS train movements in level 2.

A centralised safety unit that receives train position information via radio and sends movement authorities via radio to trains. Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: ReferenceBorderPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - ReferenceBorderPoint

models.name: RunningTrack
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA RINF - RunningTrack
models.description: Running track (era:RunningTrack's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A running track means any track used for train service movements; passing loops and meeting loops on plain line or track connections only required for train operation are not published Inherits attributes from era:Track/era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: Siding

Safe Area: Area defined by the Infrastructure Manager where it is safe or suitable to stop and evacuate a train.
Industrial Risk Area: locations where it is dangerous for the driver to step out. Inherits attributes from era:InfrastructureElement/era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

It may be also a non-rail point or a rail point that is not managed by an Infrastructure Manager (IM). It may be defined by entity having company code according to their needs. The Subsidiary location is optional and dependent upon business needs. Inherits attributes from era:Feature (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

title: Accidentes de Tráfico de la Ciudad de Madrid (Traffic Accidents in the City of Madrid)
description: Traffic accidents in the City of Madrid with victims and/or municipal property damage, registered by Policía Municipal. Sourced from a PDF field specification (in Spanish) rather than a formal ontology -- this candidate was built directly from that specification and cross-checked against the real, published CSV dataset for the year 2023.
publisher: Dirección General de la Policía Municipal, Ayuntamiento de Madrid
license: Not stated in the source PDF specification. The Madrid open data portal's general terms of use should be checked before promoting this candidate; not verified as part of this translation.

models.name: AccidentInvolvedPerson
models.title: Smart Data Models - Madrid Traffic Accidents - AccidentInvolvedPerson
models.description: A record of one person involved in a traffic accident in the City of Madrid, as registered by the Policia Municipal (drivers, passengers, pedestrians, witnesses). The source dataset publishes one row per involved person, not per accident -- accident-level fields (location, weather, type, coordinates) are repeated identically across every person in the same accident, which this candidate's entity design mirrors faithfully. Source: 'Accidentes de Trafico de la Ciudad de Madrid', Direccion General de la Policia Municipal, version November 2023.
